question: Eleanor Roosevelt, who was the chairperson of UDHR, belonged to which country?
solution:
The correct answer is__** USA.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Eleanor Roosevelt was an American politician, diplomat, and activist who served as the chairperson of the **United Nations Commission on Human Rights**.
 
• She played a crucial role in drafting the **Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR)**, which was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 1948.
 
• Her leadership and advocacy for human rights were pivotal in shaping international human rights standards.
 
• Eleanor Roosevelt is often regarded as one of the most influential women in American history, known for her commitment to social justice and equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Early Life**: Eleanor Roosevelt was born on October 11, 1884, in New York City and came from a prominent family. She was educated in private schools and traveled extensively.
 
• **Political Career**: She served as the First Lady of the United States from 1933 to 1945, during her husband Franklin D. Roosevelt's presidency, where she redefined the role of the First Lady by actively engaging in political and social issues.
 
• She was appointed to the UN General Assembly in 1946 by President Harry S. Truman.
 
• **Human Rights Advocacy**: After her husband's death, she continued to advocate for civil rights, women's rights, and international human rights, serving as a delegate to the United Nations.
 
• **Legacy**: Eleanor Roosevelt's contributions to human rights are celebrated globally, and her work on the UDHR remains a cornerstone of modern human rights law.
